name: Besodja
title: Father of Meshullam, a wall repairer in Jerusalem
summary: Besodja is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as the father of Meshullam, one of those who participated in repairing the walls of Jerusalem after the exile in Babylon. He is among the many individuals briefly noted in connection with the rebuilding work under Nehemiah's leadership.

keyEvents.title: Meshullam, son of Besodja, repairs the Old Gate
keyEvents.description: Besodja's son Meshullam took part in repairing the Old Gate (the Fish Gate) in Jerusalem as part of the major rebuilding project led by Nehemiah.

keyEvents.title: The Rebuilding of Jerusalem's Walls
keyEvents.description: Nehemiah organized the people to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem, and Besodja's son was among those who took responsibility for a specific section of the wall work.

keyEvents.title: Opposition to the Rebuilding
keyEvents.description: Despite opposition from enemies such as Sanballat and Tobiah, the workers, including Besodja's son, continued to build the walls with perseverance and faith.

keyEvents.title: Completion of the Wall
keyEvents.description: The wall work was completed in just 52 days, testifying to God's help and the people's effort, including the contribution from Besodja's family.
